text:
alex_c: Hey team — noticed a spike of 500s from the analytics API and several of our console charts are stuck/blanking since ~09:20 PDT. Happening across multiple orgs. Example console: https://console.redwood.example/tenant/alpha/dashboards/42 :thinking_face:

sara_support: Thanks Alex. Can you drop the root request id (from browser devtools) when a chart fails? Also which datasets are affected?

alex_c: root id from one failure: rq_20260317_9a3f2b. Affected panels: daily-active-users, latency-p95, and the custom kpi tile that hits /analytics/query/v2. Observed on Chrome and Safari.

sam_sre: I'm seeing a matching error in the analytics proxy logs for rq_20260317_9a3f2b — 502 -> upstream timeout in 10s. Stack: analytics-proxy -> analytics-query -> clickhouse. Pasting sampled log lines:```
2026-03-17T09:20:11.623Z INFO proxy request rq_20260317_9a3f2b "POST /v2/query" latency=10.02s status=502 upstream_err="timeout"
2026-03-17T09:20:11.624Z ERROR query service failed id=qry_7b3f idx=12 err="clickhouse: timeout after 9.8s"
```

observability-bot: alert:analytics-query latency_high triggered (p95 12.4s), incident_id=INC-20260317-1123

ops_oncall: We're getting a paging alert. Is this related to the autoscale policy? Today at 09:15 we did a config roll that reduced shard count for query workers.

sam_sre: Good catch — I see autoscale events at 09:16: `scale-down workers from 12 to 6` in cluster audit. That likely reduced parallel query capacity for a burst. Replaying a sample query against a warm replica returns fine, but when we hammer with concurrent dashboard loads we hit timeouts.

jia_runtime: Can you share the exact query payload from the console tile? If it's doing full table scans we should rewrite aggregation to use the derived summary table.

sara_support: Alex — can you repro and capture devtools network timeline + the failing request body? Also include the Console UI route id (right-click panel -> copy link).

alex_c: Reproduced and attached (copied payload inline):```
POST /v2/query
{
  "dataset":"events","start":"2026-03-09","end":"2026-03-17","metrics":[{"name":"count","agg":"sum"}],"group_by":["user_id"],"limit":10000
}
```
This is heavier than the small summary query. We added it recently to show top users.

sam_sre: That group_by + high limit is likely the culprit. Two quick mitigations: 1) reduce limit to 100 or add server-side top-k aggregation, 2) pin the dashboard route to use summary dataset (there's a config on the tile).

jia_runtime: On the runtime side I'll add a temporary fallback route that serves a cached summary when analytics-query latency > 5s. Also enabling query-level circuit-breaker for heavy GROUP BYs. Will push a canary in 15m.

ops_oncall: For now we should rollback the scale-down to 12 workers and throttle dashboard clients via the console proxy to reduce concurrent load. I'm doing the scale-up now.

alex_c: Thanks — scaling up and the charts recovered for me. Will update dashboard tiles to summary queries and lower limits.

sara_support: Great. Closing loop: root cause = autoscale/scale-down during burst + a couple of heavy GROUP BY dashboard tiles. Remediation: scale back, add runtime fallback, update tile queries + add dashboard lint to prevent high-cardinality group_by. Filing follow-up RFC for tile validation. :white_check_mark:
